html:
A Catholic uprising in central and western Mexico from 1926 to 1929 against the government's laws limiting the church. Its fighters were called Cristeros after their cry, "Long live Christ the King!"

The Constitution of 1917, a product of the Mexican Revolution, restricted the church: no church schools, no church property, and no foreign priests. President Plutarco Elías Calles enforced these articles harshly from 1926, with the "Calles Law". The bishops suspended public worship in protest. Peasants in states such as Jalisco, Michoacán and Guanajuato took up arms.

The war was cruel on both sides, with executions of priests and attacks on teachers and civilians. Perhaps 90,000 people died. The US ambassador Dwight Morrow helped broker a deal in 1929: the laws stayed but would not be fully enforced, and worship resumed. Many Cristeros who laid down arms were later killed. The Catholic Church has since declared dozens of its martyrs saints.
sum: A Catholic uprising in central and western Mexico from 1926 to 1929 against the government's laws limiting the church. Its fighters were called Cristeros after their cry, "Long live Christ the King!"
